title: Progress a child can read
statement: Show progress as a labelled count a child can read, such as 'Page X of Y', and name a page's internal steps rather than present them as page progress.
example: A row of about 28 page dots with no legend did not move across five content steps.
detail: A supplied UI review found a progress row of about 28 dots, too fine to count and with no legend, that did not advance across five content steps, and suggested a simple count instead (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/aladdin-p1-ui-review.reference.md`, line 21). The project found that its dots counted pages, not the steps inside a page, and replaced them with an explicit 'Page X of Y' plus named step text, never calling internal steps page progress (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md`, line 11). An independent source review accepted that page number and page purpose stay visible (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/NAVIGATION-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW-by-residual.md`, line 16).
against: The mapped change is marked "Scoped source changed; browser acceptance pending" (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md`, line 11).

evidence.quote: It did not advance across five content steps on `/p2`.
It uses about 28 dots, too fine to count and far below a usable touch size, in three shapes and colours with no legend.
Existing dots represent pages, not the substeps of vocabulary/model.
Replace in PeterPan with explicit Page X of Y and keep local named step text. Never call internal steps page progress.
Page number plus page purpose remain visible; Back sits beside the primary action.
